description: I'm an independent developer interested in space exploration, software engineering, 3D simulations and emerging technologies. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, I developed Project Shackleton, an interactive lunar outpost simulation combining 3D environments, survival systems, NASA data integration and AI-assisted communication. I enjoy tackling complex technical challenges and turning ideas into functional, interactive experiences.
summary: Project Shackleton is an interactive 3D lunar outpost simulation that explores the challenges of sustaining a human presence near the Moon's South Pole. Set on the rim of Shackleton Crater, the experience places users in the role of managing a five-person crew during a 14-day mission. Players must balance critical survival systems, including power, oxygen, water, CO₂ levels, radiation protection and crew health, while responding to changing environmental conditions and mission emergencies. By combining immersive first-person exploration, habitat and rover interactions, mission telemetry and communication systems, Project Shackleton turns the complex challenges of lunar habitation into an engaging, interactive experience. It aims to demonstrate the interconnected systems, decision-making and operational challenges involved in establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon.
details:
Project Overview

Project Shackleton is a first-person, realism-focused 3D lunar outpost simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Set on the rim of Shackleton Crater near the lunar South Pole, the project explores the operational and environmental challenges of sustaining a human presence on the Moon.

Players take the role of a mission commander responsible for keeping a five-person crew alive throughout a simulated 14-day mission. The experience combines first-person exploration, interactive habitat systems, a lunar rover and a dynamic survival simulation.

How It Works

The simulation connects several interdependent systems, including solar power generation, battery storage, oxygen supply, electrolysis, carbon dioxide scrubbing, water recycling, cabin heating, crew health and radiation exposure. Decisions made by the player affect multiple systems, requiring careful prioritisation of limited resources.

The mission features 17 types of potential emergencies, including solar storms, dust events, hull breaches, electrical fires, equipment failures and life-support malfunctions. Players must assess situations, make decisions and coordinate responses through the onboard mission tablet and communication systems.

The habitat includes interactive life-support equipment, crew facilities and operational consoles. A six-wheel pressurised lunar rover allows players to explore the surrounding terrain, navigate obstacles and manage vehicle damage and repairs.

Scientific Data and NASA Integration

Project Shackleton incorporates real lunar elevation data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), using a high-resolution 5-metre-per-pixel terrain dataset to construct the Shackleton region.

It also integrates NASA's Community Coordinated Modeling Center (CCMC) Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI). Solar-flare information influences the simulated radiation environment and contributes to mission events.

Technology and Development

The project is built using TypeScript, Three.js and Vite, with a browser-based 3D rendering and simulation architecture. Vercel is used for deployment and server-side API functionality.

Additional integrations include NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center data, Open-Meteo weather services, and BBC and NPR news feeds for the communication environment.

AI-assisted communication systems allow players to interact with Houston and individual crew members through text and voice. These systems incorporate language-model responses, speech recognition and text-to-speech functionality, with fallback responses when external AI services are unavailable.

Creativity, Benefits and Intended Impact

Rather than presenting lunar exploration as a static collection of facts, Project Shackleton turns it into an interactive operational experience. Its interconnected systems demonstrate how decisions concerning energy, life support, radiation protection and crew safety can influence one another.

The project aims to make the challenges of lunar habitation more accessible and engaging while encouraging users to think critically about resource management, emergency response and the complexity of future human exploration missions.

The simulation uses simplified and adjustable parameters for its training scenarios; it is an educational simulation rather than a certified engineering or flight-planning tool.

Acknowledgment of AI Assistance

AI tools were used during development for ideation, coding assistance, debugging and the implementation of interactive language-model-based communication and voice features. AI-assisted speech and generated media are identified where applicable. AI-generated visual and video material is distinguished with the required visible watermark.

Accessibility and Resource Considerations

The experience incorporates keyboard-based controls, on-screen captions and text-based communication alongside optional voice interactions. Energy availability, battery capacity and resource consumption are central to the simulation, encouraging users to consider the constraints of operating a lunar habitat. The simulation uses simplified training parameters and is designed as an interactive educational experience rather than a validated engineering model.
